cycles.red: the focused test could not import a snapshot-fetch boundary, monotonic clock or refresh driver because no runtime lease consumer existed
cycles.green: one generic driver now fetches once and installs a complete validated snapshot only through the exact lease

cycles.red: a failed fetch returned the transport error but left refresh_in_flight true
cycles.green: fetch failure first completes the exact lease as failed, retains last-known-good keys and then reports the closed fetch error

cycles.red: aborting a task while its fetch future was pending left the exact refresh lease stuck
cycles.green: a private RAII guard releases only its own generation when a polled future is dropped

cycles.red: dropping the refresh future before its first poll never entered the async body and left the lease stuck
cycles.green: the guard is armed synchronously before the future is returned, so even an unpolled drop completes the lease

cycles.red: the runtime crate exposed only an injected clock trait and no process-local production implementation
cycles.green: SystemJwksMonotonicClock reports bounded elapsed Instant milliseconds and exposes no wall-time value
